reason: Razumihin just quoted the mother as saying 'his girl', so the gloss should repeat the same words.

old: It was his doing — that day under the lamp in the corridor.
new: It all started that day under the lamp in the corridor.
reason: 'It was his doing' makes it sound as if Razumihin still blames Raskolnikov, which contradicts 'I wronged him'; the line refers to where Razumihin's own suspicion began.

old: Just as a man might endure half an hour of mortal terror with a robber — yet when the knife is finally at his throat, he feels no fear.
new: It was like a man who endures half an hour of mortal terror alone with a robber, yet when the knife is finally at his throat, feels no fear.
reason: The sentence is a fragment ('Just as...' with no main clause), which is hard to follow when heard.

old: There have been Wanderers in his family
new: There have been Wanderers — members of a religious sect — in his family
reason: A listener hears the translator's note only as a detached line afterwards; a short inline gloss tells them who the Wanderers are at the moment it matters.

new: because I'm such a Schiller, such a starry-eyed idealist?
reason: This is the first use of 'Schiller' as shorthand for a romantic idealist, and a listener will not know the allusion.

old: in this one is bound to go to excess
new: in this, one is bound to go to excess
reason: Without the comma, 'this one' is misread as a noun phrase.

old: She thought it showed I was unwilling to deceive her by warning her in advance
new: She thought that by warning her in advance I showed I was unwilling to deceive her
reason: The misplaced 'by warning her in advance' makes the sentence hard to follow on first hearing.
The edition glosses the other French phrases in this scene, such as 'assez causé'; this one should be glossed the same way.

new: _la nature et la vérité_ — nature and truth! Ha-ha!
